sentences.text: The Complainant has filed complaint U/Sec.200 of Code of Criminal Procedure against the Accused for the offence punishable U/Sec.138 of Negotiable Instrument Act.

2. The facts of the case in brief are as follows:-
The accused had availed various gold loans from the complainant by pledging gold in all total amounting to more than Rs.65,00,000/-.

In order to discharge part of the liability arising out of the said gold loan availed by the accused, and amongst other cheques, the accused had also issued two cheques bearing No.004911 dated 18.07.2013 drawn on Central Bank of India, Vijayanagar, Bangalore for the sum of Rs.20,00,000/- and cheque bearing No.501637 dated 18.07.2013 drawn on State bank of Mysore, Vijayanagara for the sum of Rs.20,00,000/- in favour of the complainant.

3. The complainant further submitted that they presented above said two cheques for encashment to the State Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd., Magadi Road, Bangalore the said cheque was returned dishonored on presentation with endorsement dated 12.10.2013 showing the reason "Funds Insufficient".

Therefore, complainant issued a legal notice on 30.10.2013 to the accused through his advocate calling upon the accused for the payment of the said amount due on the dishonored cheque within 15 days from the date of receipt of the said notice.
However, the accused has not made any payment.
Hence present complainant filed by the complainant.

4. After recording the sworn statement of the Regional Manager of complainant company and also verifying the documents, cognizance was taken against the accused for the offence punishable under Sec. 138 R/w 142 of N.I. Act.
The accused on receiving the summons appeared before the Court through his counsel and was enlarged on bail and his plea was recorded.
The accused pleaded not guilty, but claimed to have defence.
Hence, the case was posted for evidence of the complainant.

5. In order to prove its case, Sri.K.Subramanya Swamy, Regional Manager of the complainant company examined as PW-1 and got marked 9 documents as per Ex.P1 to 9 and he was cross-examined by the accused.
The accused got examined himself as DW1 and also got marked 33 documents at Ex.D1 to Ex.D33.
Learned counsel for the complainant cross examined DW-1.

Then,
the matter was posted for Arguments.
6. Heard the arguments on both sides.
Learned counsel for the accused filed memo with list of citations.
Perused the records.

7. The following points arise for my consideration:
1.

Whether the complainant proves that the cheques bearing No.501637 & 004911 for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- each dated: 18.07.2013 drawn on State Bank of Mysore,
Vijayanagar issued by the accused has been dishonored on the ground of "Funds Ms Muthoottu Mini Financiers P Ltd vs N B Siddaramaiah on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70702761/
2 Insufficient" and the accused even after receiving the intimation regarding the dishonor of cheque failed to pay the cheque amount within the stipulated period and thereby accused has committed an offence punishable under Sec.138 of N.I. Act?
2. What order?
8. My findings on the above points are as under Point No.1: In the Affirmative Point No.2: As per final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Point No.1 : The complainant has filed complaint u/s 138 of NI Act alleging that the accused has committed an offence punishable u/s 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act stating that accused had availed various gold loans from the complainant finance company by pledging gold in all totally amounting to more than Rs.65,00,000/-.

sentences.text: 13. The first contention of the accused is that PW-1 is not duly authorized person to represent the case.
In the cross examination of PW-1, for the suggestion of accused, PW-1 admitted that he has not produced documents with respect to registration of company.
He admitted that there is no signature of the Director in Ex.P10 and admitted that Ex.P10 is Certified copy.
Further denied the suggestion that company had not given any authorization to him.
Further admitted that Ex.P10 has been given to recover the gold and to initiate the proceedings.
The accused has disputed with regard to authorization issued by the complainant company in favour of PW-1.

In order to prove the authorization of PW-1, he has produced Certified true copy of resolution dated 22.05.2012 which authorized Mr.K.Subramanya Swami, Chief Manager of complainant company authorized to appear before all civil and criminal courts and also to file claim petition in connection with the recovery of gold and to sign vakalathnama etc., on behalf of the company.
This document is issued after the meeting of Board of Directors of complainant company.
Ex . P10
the document signed by the company secretary at the meeting of board of directors of the complainant company clearly stated that PW-1 has been appointed as authorized person to conduct the case.
This documents shows that complainant company has authorized PW-1 for conducting the case.
In the said document there is a clear recital with regard to the authorization.
Moreover if there was no authorization by the company then what is necessity for PW-1 to attend the case.
The documents produced by the complainant shows that complainant company has been appointed PW-1 as its authorized person to proceed with this case.
On perusal of Ex.P10 it discloses the same was issued by company secretary on behalf of complainant company.
It also discloses that it is the certified true copy of original.
Moreover, PW-1 has deposed that company has issued said copy only.
Therefore, he has produced the same before this court.
Therefore, the contention of the accused not tenable in the eye of law.
14. Secondly, it is another contention of the accused is that the complainant has not produced any documents to show that accused has availed loan of Rs.65,00,000/-.

It is observed that during cross Ms Muthoottu Mini Financiers P Ltd vs N B Siddaramaiah on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70702761/

then the manager will fix the quantum of loan.

sentences.text: Further deposed that he has not produced documents even the company maintains books, receipt book.
Further deposed that accused availed Rs.65,00,000/- gold loan on different dates and also has documents with respect of loan took by accused.
Further admitted the suggestion of accused that he has not having any problem to produce the said documents.
Denied the suggestion of accused that he is adducing false evidence stating about accused had availed gold loan of Rs.65 lakh.

With this regard, it is observed that during chief examination of DW-1, he admitted that he had pledged gold ornaments in the complainant company for availing loan and also use to take the gold loan whenever he was in need.

The accused contention is that complainant company has not produced any relevant document to show that accused has availed loan for Rs.65,00,000/- but he admitted that he availed loan from the complainant company as per Ex.D5 to Ex.D32.
Ex.D5 to Ex.D32 are the customer receipts issued by complainant company in favour of present accused with regard to pledging of gold under various loan number since 26.04.2012 to 01.04.2013.

If really accused wanted to prove that he has not availed loan of Rs.65 lakh from the complainant company he could have summon the documents from the complainant company showing the transaction of Rs.65 lakh between himself with the complainant company but accused has not done the same.
What prevented the accused to call for those documents if really those are necessary to prove his case.

No doubt PW-1 has deposed that he has having document for having lent an amount of Rs.65 lakh to the accused and he also deposed that he has not produced the said document either at the time of filing complaint or at the time of filing of chief examination affidavit.

No doubt PW1 has not produced documents to show lending of gold loan to the extent of Rs.65 lakh to the accused but whereas accused himself admitted the pledging of gold and borrowing of loan from the complainant in the year 2013 to 2014.
When the accused himself admitted the loan transaction between himself and complainant, the non production of document by the complainant is not fatal to the case of the complainant.
Therefore, in view of provisions of evidence act facts admitted need not be proved.
Hence, contention of the accused is not tenable in the eye of law.
15. Thirdly, the another contention of the accused is on 06.06.2013 complainant have collected 6 cheques at police station of different bank.

During the argument counsel for the complainant stated that the cheques in question were given for discharge of legal liability but counsel for the accused argued that complainant took the cheques forcibly in the police station by threatening him.

With this regard, during cross of PW-1, the complainant deposed that on 18.07.2013, accused has given two cheques in his office and further deposed that apart from the two cheques the accused has not given any other cheques and also given the instruction to present the cheque for encashment on 10.10.2013.

Furthermore, denied the suggestion of accused that he is deposing falsely that accused had given the cheques in question on 18.07.2013 and also not given any instruction and also not given information about the return of cheques to accused.

16. Further denied the suggestion that on 06.06.2013, police have pressurized the accused at police station, made him to write a statement and forcibly obtained 6 cheques from him, which the police have given the same to the complainant.
Further PW-1 denied that Ex.P1 & Ex.P2 are obtained at the police station on 06.06.2013.

Further denied the suggestion that Ex.P1 & Ex.P2 not given by the accused on 18.07.2013 and accused has not availed gold loan of Rs.65 lakh and also denied that he Ms Muthoottu Mini Financiers P Ltd vs N B Siddaramaiah on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70702761/

sentences.text: It is observed that during the chief examination of DW-1, the accused deposed that he had not given cheques in question for discharge of legal lability.
The Kamakshipalya police took him to police station and threatened him on 03.05.2013 and took 6 cheques from him and also obtained his signature in one document.
17. Further deposed that he had mentioned the cheque number in the said document.
Further deposed that they have taken 3 cheques of State Bank of India even though he said that the said cheques were not in force.
Further denied the suggestion of complainant that he had issued cheques in question towards part payment and admitted his signature on the said cheques.
Further denied the suggestion that he had not given the cheques in question to repay the said gold loan.
18. On perusal of the oral and documentary evidence, the accused has availed a loan from the complainant company by pledging the gold ornaments.

Further it is noticed by the documents produced by the accused that as per final report submitted by Kamakshipalya PS wherein it is alleged that the accused has pledged counterfiet gold articles and obtained loan from the complainant company.

The Certified copy of exhibits produced by accused marked at Ex.D2 to Ex.D4 are the certified copies of final report submitted by Kamakshipalya Ps, Bengaluru, Ex.D3 and Ex.D4 are the letter correspondence made by accused to the complainant company in the form of undertaking to repay loan borrowed by him from the complainant.
As per the Ex.D3 & 4 it can be seen that the accused has made correspondence with the complainant on 30.05.2013 & 06.06.2013 admitting his liability and repayment of the same with interest.
The said letters were given to the complainant as per the dates mentioned thereon.
As per averments of final report marked at Ex.D2 it discloses that one Vishwanath Rao, Regional Manager of the complainant company visited the branch of complainant on 30.05.2013.
On his verification he found that the present accused pledged counterfeit gold ornaments and borrowed loan of Rs.66,00,47,88/- from various loan accounts.
Thereafter, said Vishwanath Rao has intimated the present complainant to file complaint against the accused and their officials for having committed criminal breach of trust and spurious ornaments.
As per the directions of Vishwanath Rao, the present complainant has lodged first information statement before Kamakshipalya PS on 12.11.2014.
Based on first information statement crime was registered against present accused and 4 others u/s 406, 408, 420, 120(B) r/w 34 of IPC.
Ex.D3 & 4 are the letter correspondence made by accused with complainant on 30.05.2013 and 06.06.2013.
For having received the said letters the complainant have put their seal on those letters.
Further at the time of investigation by Kamakshipalya PS the complainant has handed over those letter correspondence made by accused.

For having received the statement handed over by complainant,
the police have put their signature on Ex.D3.
19.
The documents produced by accused himself clearly goes to show that the complainant has lodged first information before police on 12.11.2014.
The letter correspondence made by accused is on 30.05.2013 and 06.06.2013.
When the crime was registered in the month of November 2014 how could the Kamakshipalya PS called the accused on 30.05.2013 and 06.06.2013 as alleged by the accused.
Moreover PW-1 has totally denied the contention of accused that the police have handed over the cheques in question to the complainant at Police station.

It is not the case of accused that before registering crime the police have called him and took the alleged cheques in question forcibly Ms Muthoottu Mini Financiers P Ltd vs N B Siddaramaiah on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70702761/
6 and handed over the same to the complainant.

sentences.text: It is also not forthcoming from the documents produced by the accused that the complainant have took the cheques in question at police station forcibly from the accused.

Therefore, the documents produced by the accused at Ex.D3 & 4 clearly discloses that the accused by admitting his liability has made letter correspondence with the complainant on 03.05.2013 & 06.06.2013 i.e., much earlier to the registration of crime before Kamakshipalya PS against accused.

Therefore, the contention of accused that from 30.05.2013 to 06.06.2013, the police have made him to come to the police station and forcibly took the cheque in question and handed over the same to the complainant cannot be believed.

According to the accused, if really the cheques in question were obtained in police station by threatening him, in this regard, he should have taken legal action against the police and complainant then and there only.

But it is admitted during cross examination of accused that "

 ".
Accused himself admitted that he has not given any complaint with respect of alleged threatening and obtaining of 6 cheques at the police station to the higher authority.
What prevented the accused to give the complaint if he has really gone through the same.

It is clearly goes to show that when the complainant came to know about the gold pledged by the accused are spurious and low quality, they have given complaint in this regard to Kamakshipalya police station in Cr.No.462/2014 against the present accused and others who are the employees of the said complainant company.
It is contended by accused that the Kamakshipaly police have forcibly took cheques from him and handed over the same to the complainant.
At the same time the police have also obtained his signature on one statement.
In order to substantiate the same he has relied upon Ex.D2 final report.

At page No.31 of final report it could be seen the police have recorded voluntarily statement of accused on 13.12.2014 and obtained the signature of accused thereon during the course of investigation.

Accused has not placed any document on record to prove his contention that since 30.05.2013 to 06.06.2013, Kamakshipalya police have made the accused to come to police station and thereon police have obtained cheques in question and handed over the same to the complainant.
The documents i.e., certified copy of final report marked at Ex.D2 produced by accused himself discloses that the Kamakshipalya police have recorded voluntary statement of accused on 13.12.2014.
After receipt of certified copy of said documents the accused has overwritten the month in voluntary statement to show that the same was recorded on 13.11.2014.

Even assuming for the sake of discussion that the police have recorded his statement on 13.11.2014 but the defence of accused is that the police have made him to come to the police station in between 30.05.2013 to 06.06.2013 and obtained cheques in question and obtained his signature on the statement.
When that being so the oral evidence deposed by the accused and documents placed on record are contradictory to each other.
Therefore, the defence of accused that the police have obtained cheques in question in between 30.05.2013 to 06.06.2013 and handed over the same to the complainant cannot be believable.
20. Though the accused has deposed that the cheques in question ie., State Bank of Mysore issued by him was not in force at the time when he issued said cheque to the complainant.

In order to substantiate the same he has produced statement of accounts marked at Ex.D33 pertaining to State Bank of Mysore, Vijayanagar branch, Bengaluru wherein they discloses that the accused transacted Ms Muthoottu Mini Financiers P Ltd vs N B Siddaramaiah on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70702761/
7 from said bank from 2005 to 2010.

sentences.text: In order to prove that in the year 2012-13, the said bank account was not in force, he has not produced any statement with respect to particular period.
Moreover, the cheques in question pertains to State Bank of Mysore also returned with an endorsement "Funds Insufficient".

If the said account is not in force, then the said cheque in question should have return with an endorsement "Account closed/account not in use" but in the present case said cheque returned with an endorsement funds insufficient.
As such, the contention of the accused not tenable in the eye of law.

21. It is forthcoming oral and documentary evidence that the complainant has lent gold loan to the accused and accused has pledged the gold to the complainant and borrowed gold loan on various occasions and accounts.
It is not seriously disputed by the accused about receipt of gold loan by pledging gold articles.
It is only disputed the quantum of lending gold loan to the extent of Rs.65 lakh.
From the evidence of DW-1, it could be seen that he admitted the loan transaction with complainant.
It is not his case that he has repaid entire loan amount or the gold articles pledged by him were auctioned by the complainant and same proceeds have been adjusted towards his loan.

Except the suggestion during cross of PW-1 "

.65       


 
 
 
   
    
 

 
  




 


 
 
  

 
  

 

 



   
  
 ".
Moreover it is not the case of complainant that they have auctioned the gold pledged by accused and adjusted the same to the loan of accused.
Therefore, from the oral evidence on record it could be seen that no evidence led by the accused to prove repayment of loan borrowed by him to the complainant.
Therefore, the amount claimed by the complainant is legally enforceable debt payable by accused.

22. It is borne out from the cross examination of PW-1 that he deposed that he himself wrote the contents of Ex.P1 & 2 and further deposed that as the accused told that he does not know to write, he himself wrote the said cheques.
Further he admitted the suggestion of accused, that he did not mentioned the same in the averments of the complaint, notice and in the affidavit.
As per the oral and documentary evidence, the cheques in issue were signed by the accused and the said cheques belongs to the account's of accused.
Nowhere the accused denied his signature on the said cheques.

If the accused claims that the cheque was not written by him, but it was written by complainant itself the accused may still be liable u/s 138 of NI Act if the cheque is valid, duly signed by the accused, and intended for the discharge of a debt.
The fact that complainant filled the cheque is generally not a defence if the cheque was duly authorized and signed by the accused.
Moreover during the cross examination of DW-1, accused has admitted the signature on Ex.P1 & 2 and its issuance.

It is to be noted that, Sec.20 of Negotiable Instrument Act - Says that: "the instruments may be wholly blank or incomplete in particular in either case, the holder has authority to make or complete the instrument as negotiable one".

as per Sec.20 of the Negotiable Instruments Act the contents of cheque can be filled-up by the complainant himself and even though if the contents of Ex.P1 & 2 cheques are not written by accused the same is of no consequence and the accused cannot take advantage of the same without he placing credible evidence before the court that the Ex.P1 & 2 cheques were not issued by him towards discharge of legally enforceable debt.
Therefore the contention of the accused is not tenable in the eye of law.
The citation relied by the accused is not applicable to the present case in hand.

sentences.text: As observed above, it has to be presumed that the cheques in question were issued by the accused to discharge the legal recoverable debt.
The accused can place rebuttable evidence so as to show that the cheques were not issued for repayment of loan amount.
As the accused has failed to put acceptable and satisfactory evidence to probablise the debt.
Therefore, there is no question of saying the cheques were not issued for liability.

Further it is not disputed that cheques in question bears his signature and they pertains to his accounts maintained at State Bank of Mysore,
Vijayanagar.
Since he has not denied the signature on the cheques and the said cheques were dishonored.
Hence accused has committed office punishable u/s 138 of NI Act.
24. The accused has utterly failed to prove his defence that the cheque issued by the accused is forcibly at the police station not towards the legal lability.
The accused has failed to satisfy this court with the cogent and convincing materials.
The accused has utterly failed to prove his defence .
Hence, the case of the complainant is believable one since the complainant has proved his case beyond reasonable doubts.
Hence, in view of this I answer Point No.1 In the Affirmative.
25. POINT NO.2:-

In view of my answer to Point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER

In exercise of power conferred U/sec. 255(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure,
the accused is convicted for the offence punishable U/s.138 of N.I. Act and sentenced to pay fine of Rs.61,60,000/-.
In default of payment of the said fine amount, the accused shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of Six months.

Out of the fine amount Rs.61,59,000/- shall be paid to the complainant as compensation as contemplated U/sec.357(1)(b) of Code of Criminal Procedure and the remaining fine amount of Rs.1,000/- shall be paid to the state.
The Judgment copy shall be supplied to the accused on free of cost.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When that being so the oral evidence deposed by the accused and documents placed on record are contradictory to each other.
Therefore, the defence of accused that the police have obtained cheques in question in between 30.05.2013 to 06.06.2013 and handed over the same to the complainant cannot be believable.
In order to prove that in the year 2012-13, the said bank account was not in force, he has not produced any statement with respect to particular period.
Moreover, the cheques in question pertains to State Bank of Mysore also returned with an endorsement "Funds Insufficient".
If the said account is not in force, then the said cheque in question should have return with an endorsement "Account closed/account not in use" but in the present case said cheque returned with an endorsement funds insufficient.
It is only disputed the quantum of lending gold loan to the extent of Rs.65 lakh.
The fact that complainant filled the cheque is generally not a defence if the cheque was duly authorized and signed by the accused.
as per Sec.20 of the Negotiable Instruments Act the contents of cheque can be filled-up by the complainant himself and even though if the contents of Ex.P1 & 2 cheques are not written by accused the same is of no consequence and the accused cannot take advantage of the same without he placing credible evidence before the court that the Ex.P1 & 2 cheques were not issued by him towards discharge of legally enforceable debt.
The citation relied by the accused is not applicable to the present case in hand.
Ms Muthoottu Mini Financiers P Ltd vs N B Siddaramaiah on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70702761/
8 23.
As observed above, it has to be presumed that the cheques in question were issued by the accused to discharge the legal recoverable debt.
The accused can place rebuttable evidence so as to show that the cheques were not issued for repayment of loan amount.
As the accused has failed to put acceptable and satisfactory evidence to probablise the debt.
Therefore, there is no question of saying the cheques were not issued for liability.
Further it is not disputed that cheques in question bears his signature and they pertains to his accounts maintained at State Bank of Mysore,
Vijayanagar.
Since he has not denied the signature on the cheques and the said cheques were dishonored.
Hence accused has committed office punishable u/s 138 of NI Act.
24. The accused has utterly failed to prove his defence that the cheque issued by the accused is forcibly at the police station not towards the legal lability.
The accused has failed to satisfy this court with the cogent and convincing materials.
The accused has utterly failed to prove his defence .
Hence, the case of the complainant is believable one since the complainant has proved his case beyond reasonable doubts.
opennyai_summary.decision:
25. POINT NO.2:-
In view of my answer to Point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
In exercise of power conferred U/sec. 255(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure,
the accused is convicted for the offence punishable U/s.138 of N.I. Act and sentenced to pay fine of Rs.61,60,000/-.
In default of payment of the said fine amount, the accused shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of Six months.
Out of the fine amount Rs.61,59,000/- shall be paid to the complainant as compensation as contemplated U/sec.357(1)(b) of Code of Criminal Procedure and the remaining fine amount of Rs.1,000/- shall be paid to the state.
The Judgment copy shall be supplied to the accused on free of cost.
